transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-01 | Start: 16:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 mins
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Jamie Park (Redwood AE), Riley Nguyen (Redwood SE), Aisha Conte (CSM) — Dr. Lena Ortiz, Samir Patel, Olivia Chen, Marcus Hale (Mistral Therapeutics)

Summary:
Quick operational check-in ahead of pilot kickoff. Covered current usage patterns, cost hotspots (high short-sequence embedding churn and inference spikes), latency SLOs, dedicated vs hosted trade-offs, and security checklist (SOC2, SSO, KMS). Agreed next steps: run 24h benchmark, draft pricing, gather traffic profile, and schedule pilot start on 2026-11-10.

Topics: usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents (recent 10/24 latency blip), roadmap alignment for holiday surge, security/compliance requirements, pilot scope and success criteria.

Action items (captured live): see metadata section.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Jamie Park: Alright everybody, thanks for carving time today. Quick intros — I'll be leading the account side, Riley will handle the perf and ops questions, and Aisha on CSM. Over to you Lena for quick context on today's priorities.
[00:20] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Sure, thanks. High-level: we're about to flip a customer-facing inference feature into beta and want to validate cost/latency under production load. We had a spike end of October where p99 jumped to 1.4s and some tails, so main goals are: keep p95 < 300ms, p99 < 800ms for gen endpoints, and contain cost growth. Also need security checks before pilot.
[01:05] Riley Nguyen: Got it. Can I ask — is that on hosted or your private infra?
[01:10] Samir Patel: Right now it's hosted with a mix of our infra for data enrichment; we're evaluating dedicated Redwood capacity because of the consistent throughput. We don't want to self-manage the KV cache logic and scaling right now.
[01:30] Riley Nguyen: OK. For dedicated vs hosted the main tradeoffs are predictability and isolation vs flexibility and lower up-front commit. We can do canary rollouts and autoscale on Dedicated but you get better unit economics when workload shapes match reserved pools.
[01:55] Olivia Chen: One other constraint: we require VPC peering for any private routes, and we need KMS integration for encryption-in-transit and at-rest keys. Also SAML SSO with RBAC needs to map to our AD groups.
[02:20] Aisha Conte: Noted — we'll attach our KMS + SAML checklist. On SOC2 docs, we can share the latest audit artifact and the control mapping for data residency.
[02:40] Marcus Hale: From product side, success criteria for pilot are: 95th percentile latency <= 300ms, cost per 1k tokens under $X (we discussed a target range), and no more than 1 customer-visible error per week. If we hit those, we'll expand feature rollout.
[03:05] Riley Nguyen: Understood. For the cost target, can you confirm current baseline — token mix, average sequence length, and embedding churn?
[03:20] Samir Patel: Avg seq length is pretty short — ~22 tokens for quick responses, embeddings churn is high because we re-embed on session change, roughly 18M embeddings a month. We can provide raw numbers after the call.
[03:45] Riley Nguyen: That explains it. High embedding churn plus short generations is a classic cost hotspot — batching helps less for embeddings because they're per-user, but KV cache and prefix caching will help gen cost. We also recommended quantized variants for part of the model; that drops token cost ~25-40% in our experience with modest latency impact.
[04:30] Dr. Lena Ortiz: How mature is your quantization pipeline? We need stability — if quality drops, product can't ship.
[04:45] Riley Nguyen: We have vetted q4_0 and int8-like profiles for several open models. We'll run the quality regression against your eval set as part of the benchmark. If the regression exceeds your threshold we won't promote that profile for the pilot.
[05:10] Jamie Park: Quick note on reliability — the 10/24 blip was a region failover plus transient queueing. We have automated fallbacks that route to a compatible variant; there was an interaction with bucketed autoscaling that exacerbated the tail. We're proposing a two-step: 1) pilot with routed fallbacks enabled; 2) tighter autoscale thresholds and batch-size caps for the first 72h.
[05:40] Olivia Chen: Can those fallbacks preserve token semantics? We can't have inconsistent outputs between primary and fallback models.
[05:50] Riley Nguyen: Good call. Fallbacks are configured to use a model variant with matched temperature/decoder settings. There can be minor differences due to model architecture but we can pin model versions and include a checksum guard for regressions; if there's a detected regression we can auto-failover to a read-only mode.
[06:20] Marcus Hale: On observability — we need token-level cost and per-route latency. Does Redwood expose a per-route burn report and traces we can ingest?
[06:30] Aisha Conte: Yes — console exports per-route metrics and we can forward traces. We'll set up a read-only analytics token for Mistral to pull daily exports.
[06:45] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Security quick Q: do you support explicit KMS key rotation schedule and HSM backed keys?
[06:55] Jamie Park: Yes, KMS integrations support both cloud KMS and external HSM. We'll capture the details and include contact for our security engineer.
[07:10] Samir Patel: For the benchmark, we'll need to run the workload against a dedicated pool and against your hosted profile to compare unit economics. Any sample configs you recommend?
[07:25] Riley Nguyen: We'll provide a recommended workload driver (small stress script + realistic distribution based on session traces). We'll also provide an infra overlay for the dedicated pool with autoscale settings.
[07:40] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Timeline question — if we start pilot 11/10, what's the minimal runway to get representative data?
[07:50] Riley Nguyen: Minimum 72h for steady-state metrics, we prefer 7 days to capture diurnal patterns and an end-to-end cost calc. For embeddings heavy workloads might need full billing cycle to see tail costs but 7 days gives a reliable projection.
[08:10] Jamie Park: So proposed plan: run 24h controlled benchmark next week, then pilot kickoff 11/10 for 7 days. We'll review on 11/18. Does that align?
[08:22] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Yes.
[08:26] Olivia Chen: I have a question about network egress and peering costs — will those be reflected separately? We need line-itemization for chargebacks.
[08:34] Jamie Park: We can separate egress and compute. The billing export will include per-route egress tags so you can map costs. We'll also provide an estimated egress model for the pilot.
[08:50] Marcus Hale: Okay — about the p99 tail — any immediate mitigations besides autoscale? We've seen retries in our client causing amplification.
[09:00] Riley Nguyen: Rate-limiting and client-side jitter helps. Also we can use adaptive batching and priority lanes for small fast requests to avoid queue head-of-line blocking. We'll propose a two-queue model in the pilot overlay.
[09:25] Samir Patel: Are there documented SLO gates for canary failures and automatic rollback? We want that for product safety.
[09:33] Aisha Conte: Yes — our rollout system supports canary thresholds by error-rate and latency regressions and will auto-roll back if thresholds exceeded. We'll provide the canary policy template.
[09:45] Dr. Lena Ortiz: On the evaluation front, we'll share an eval set (500 prompts) that mimics our customer queries; please run quality regression and include human pass/fail counts.
[09:58] Riley Nguyen: Agreed. We'll run both automated metric checks (BLEU-ish, embedding-sim, heuristic checks) and a small human eval sample for close calls.
[10:15] Marcus Hale: Competitor check — Samir asked earlier if you've seen Anthropic or OpenAI comparisons on similar workloads.
[10:22] Jamie Park: We can share anonymized bench slides. In many cases, model choice and runtime optimizations matter more than provider; we'll include a competitive appendix with rough unit-cost delta.
[10:35] Olivia Chen: Any compliance paperwork ahead of pilot? We need SOC2, data flow diagrams, and a BAA draft.
[10:45] Jamie Park: We'll attach SOC2 artifact, DFDs, and a BAA draft to the follow-up email. Aisha will own that.
[11:00] Dr. Lena Ortiz: One small ask — for the pilot can you limit model rollouts to a pinned version so we don't get unexpected model drift?
[11:08] Riley Nguyen: Absolutely — pinning is standard for pilot; we'll create a pinned model alias and only apply changes via the rollout policy.
[11:20] Samir Patel: Ok great. On capacity sizing, what's your suggestion for buffer? We will likely see 2x baseline during feature release.
[11:29] Riley Nguyen: Recommend 1.5–2x reserved with burst headroom. If you want cost minimization we can lean to dynamic scaling but with reserved capacity for critical lanes.
[11:43] Marcus Hale: Final check — who from Redwood will I contact on incident drills?
[11:50] Aisha Conte: That's me for operational handoffs, Riley is SE on-call during the pilot, and Jamie coordinates the account. We'll run an incident playbook review before pilot.
[12:05] Jamie Park: Alright let's recap next steps and deadlines
[12:12] Dr. Lena Ortiz: Sounds good.

Recap (live):
- Riley to run 24h benchmark against dedicated + hosted configs and share perf/cost spreadsheet + raw traces (due 2026-11-08).
- Olivia to export traffic profile (p95/p99, rps, embedding counts) and VPC constraints (due 2026-11-03).
- Jamie to send dedicated capacity pricing tiers, sample SLO ladder, SOC2 artifacts, and BAA draft (due 2026-11-05).
- Aisha to schedule pilot kickoff 2026-11-10 and invite security reviewer (due 2026-11-04).

Shared artifacts mentioned: pilot-benchmark-driver.tar.gz (will be shared via secure link), Mistral-pilot-bench.xlsx (perf sheet link to be attached), SOC2-Redwood-2026.pdf (audit artifact).

End of call 16:48 UTC.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-attribution and filler words; speaker turns approximate. There were several instances of overlapping talk during the reliability discussion.
